title: everyone has one
subtitle: the voice that narrates the day

steps.text: let's start with something most people have: an inner voice.
it's the voice that narrates the day. it reminds, it plans, it comments on how things are going.

options.label: all day
options.reply: a busy one. that's really common.

options.label: sometimes
options.reply: makes sense. it comes and goes for most people.

options.label: not sure
options.reply: that's a good place to start. we'll listen for it together.

steps.text: psychologists have studied inner speech for nearly a century. a large 2015 review found it's a common part of thinking: it helps us plan, remember, and get through hard moments.
steps.evidence: strong that inner speech is common; it varies a lot between people

steps.text: some people hear a lot of it, some barely any. both are normal. and it isn't always full sentences.

steps.prompt: which of these sound like your inner voice?
steps.reply: every one of those counts. that's your inner voice at work.

steps.text: here's the part we'll keep coming back to: the inner voice learned how to talk somewhere. it isn't the only way to talk inward.
most people have an inner voice. it's a habit of talking, and habits can grow.
steps.evidence: strong that inner speech is common; it varies a lot between people

steps.text: once today, just notice your inner voice. no need to change anything.

grounding.idea: inner speech is a common part of everyday thinking, used for planning, memory and self-regulation
